intro: I inherited a 48-slide investor prospectus crammed with dense tables and boilerplate copy. Working solo and on a tight clock, I rebuilt the narrative around three C-suite questions: risk, return, and timeline. I merged the Excel data into branded charts, introduced iconography, and tightened the flow to 16 slides. The pages walk investors through market comps on a map, leasing and market summaries, demand drivers, the region, the loan request, and a project cost breakdown. Clean white pages, bold headings, and architectural renderings and location photography give the numbers room to read. The cleaner deck secured three additional lenders and advanced a $16.5 M development to the term-sheet stage. Along the way I demonstrated rapid, low-touch iteration, executive storytelling, and data-driven design.
